chunks: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله heard a woman insulting a servant-girl of hers while she was fasting. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله called for food and said to her, “Eat.”
She said, “Indeed I am fasting.” He said, “How can you be fasting when you have insulted your servant-girl? Indeed, fasting is not only from food and drink.”

key_terms.الشَّرَابِ: Drink, from which the fasting person abstains.
key_terms.الصَّوْمَ: Fasting, understood here in its fuller spiritual and ethical sense.
key_terms.الطَّعَامِ: Food, from which the fasting person abstains.
key_terms.تَسُبُّ: She insults or reviles; abusive speech.
key_terms.جَارِيَةً: A female servant or bondwoman in this context.
key_terms.صَائِمَةٌ: A woman who is observing the fast.
key_terms.كُلِي: Eat; an imperative command addressed to a woman.

ai.seo_question: Is fasting only abstaining from food and drink, or does it also require avoiding insults and bad speech?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the reality of sawm (fasting) is not limited to abstaining from food and drink. It also requires moral restraint, including guarding the tongue from abuse and insults. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله highlights that wrongful speech undermines the spiritual purpose of fasting.
